why_now.industry_shift: Remote freelancing and distributed agency models rely heavily on clear asynchronous updates and structured communication over endless meetings.
why_now.ai_impact: AI tools can rapidly draft messages, but human judgment, empathy, accountability, and cultural tact are essential to preserve client trust.
why_now.business_demand: Poor communication, vague commitments, and mismanaged scope are the leading reasons service providers lose clients and damage reputations.
why_now.career_opportunity: Professionals with structured communication and coordination skills build longer client relationships, win referrals, and manage projects smoothly.

responsible_ai_communication.heading: Write Smarter With AI. Take Responsibility for Every Client Promise.
responsible_ai_communication.copy: Learn to use AI tools to improve message clarity, organize meeting notes and prepare professional updates while verifying every statement. Develop a responsible workflow that protects client information, respects cultural context and keeps people accountable for project commitments.
appropriate_uses: Refining message tone and improving conciseness
Simplifying complex technical explanations for non-technical clients
Summarizing approved meeting notes into action items
Formatting weekly status reports into consistent templates
Identifying ambiguities or unstated assumptions in client briefs
Generating alternative de-escalation phrasing for sensitive emails
Drafting structured escalation summaries for leadership review
prohibited_practices: Inventing meeting decisions or unconfirmed agreements
Misrepresenting project progress or completion status
Promising unauthorized discounts, refunds, or concessions
Committing to unrealistic delivery dates without team verification
Uploading confidential client files into unauthorized AI platforms
Generating aggressive, manipulative, or deceptive responses
Concealing serious project delays or quality defects
responsible_ai_communication.ai_drafting_prompt_example: Review this fictional client update for clarity, professional tone and actionability. Preserve every confirmed fact, deadline and responsibility. Do not invent commitments, approvals, completion dates, costs or project status. Flag any statement that needs human verification before sending.

privacy_and_security.heading: Protect Client Information While Communicating Professionally.
privacy_and_security.confidentiality_guidelines: Never share private client files, credentials, financial details, or internal communications via unrestricted links. Apply data minimization in all communications.
privacy_and_security.recording_privacy: Screen recordings must shield confidential desktop notifications, personal tabs, and sensitive project assets. Links must be restricted to authorized stakeholders.
privacy_and_security.meeting_consent: Meeting recording and AI note-taking require explicit informed consent from all participants prior to activation.

coordination_framework.heading: Keep Every Client Conversation Clear, Documented and Actionable.
components: Communication Record: Date, channel, topic, key decisions, open questions, and next steps.
Action Register: Action item, designated owner, status, confirmed due date, and dependencies.
Feedback Register: Feedback item, stakeholder source, deliverable version, requested change, and resolution.
Risk & Blocker Log: Problem description, business impact, proposed recovery options, and decision owner.
Handover Checklist: Deliverable files, usage instructions, open items, support boundaries, and final sign-off.

ideal_for: Agency account coordinators and client services assistants
Graphic designers, UI/UX designers, and video editors managing revisions
Web developers, software consultants, and digital marketing specialists
Junior project coordinators and client-facing service professionals
Small business operators and consultants communicating with clients
not_for: Individuals seeking enterprise project management certification (PMP/PRINCE2)
Professionals looking exclusively for sales negotiation or legal contract drafting
target_audience.who_should_take_foundation_first: Students with basic professional email literacy can enroll directly. Previous client experience is helpful but not mandatory.

prerequisites.required: Basic business communication ability and computer literacy. Ability to read and write simple professional messages in English. No coding required.
prerequisites.recommended: Familiarity with general workplace collaboration tools. Real client experience is not required; simulated briefs are provided.
prerequisites.hardware: A computer or laptop with working internet connection, microphone, and browser.
prerequisites.software_accounts: Access to an email client, Google Meet, Google Docs, an accessible screen recorder (Loom or free equivalent), and an AI writing assistant (ChatGPT / Gemini).

component_01.title: Component 01: Client Communication Policy
component_01.description: Communication standards, preferred channels, response expectations, business hours, urgent issue procedure, meeting etiquette, confidentiality guidelines, responsibilities, and escalation process.

component_02.title: Component 02: Onboarding Messages
component_02.description: Initial enquiry acknowledgment, professional welcome email, discovery question template, kickoff meeting invitation and agenda, and summary of next steps.

component_03.title: Component 03: Meeting Notes & Action Register
component_03.description: Kickoff meeting record, date, simulated roles, discussion summary, confirmed decisions, action items table with owners and due dates, open questions, and follow-up message.

component_04.title: Component 04: Weekly Progress Updates
component_04.description: At least two progress reports following the Completed → In Progress → Next → Blockers → Client Action Required structure.

component_05.title: Component 05: Asynchronous Update
component_05.description: A focused project update delivered via screen recording (Loom or equivalent), annotated visual walkthrough, or approved equivalent demonstration.

component_06.title: Component 06: Revision-Request Response Kit
component_06.description: Reusable response templates: acknowledging feedback, clarifying ambiguous revisions, confirming agreed changes, explaining unapproved extra requests, and notifying revision completion.

component_07.title: Component 07: Escalation & Difficult Conversations
component_07.description: Templates for scope-change responses, project delay notifications, quality concern handling, internal escalation summaries, and professional boundary-setting messages.

component_08.title: Component 08: Final Client Handover
component_08.description: Project completion message, deliverables checklist, access/file instructions, completed revisions log, outstanding items, usage guidance, handover date, support boundaries, and confirmation request.

simulated_interaction.scenario: A small business hires a freelancer or agency to deliver a creative or digital service (brand identity, social package, landing page, promotional video, or presentation package).

skill_boundaries.course_82_client_communication: Course 82 focuses specifically on professional client communication, onboarding, discovery calls, kickoff summaries, asynchronous status updates, basic task coordination, feedback and revision handling, scope-change discussions, difficult conversations, escalation, and client handover.
skill_boundaries.proposal_writing_separate: Proposal Writing is a separate certification focusing on formal business proposals, client pitches, formal scopes, pricing strategies, commercial estimates, and competitive bids.
skill_boundaries.contract_negotiation_separate: Commercial contract negotiation, legal contract interpretation, and binding agreement drafting are separate legal/sales specializations outside Course 82.
skill_boundaries.agency_operations_separate: Agency business operations, team capacity planning, financial budgeting, and agency-level management are separate advanced operational disciplines.
skill_boundaries.general_project_management_separate: Advanced project management certifications (PMP, PRINCE2, enterprise Agile/Scrum, advanced Gantt scheduling, PMO processes) are outside the scope of this communication course.
explicit_exclusions: Full business proposal writing and bid pricing
Commercial contract negotiation and legal agreements
Full agency financial and team operations
Advanced enterprise project management (PMP, Scrum Master, PRINCE2)
Guaranteed client acquisition, revenue, or retention outcomes

career_paths.employer_expectations: Professional written and verbal clarity, realistic expectation setting, thorough documentation, constructive feedback management, and accountability under pressure.
career_paths.what_student_demonstrates: Ability to onboard clients smoothly, coordinate project tasks, produce concise status reports, manage scope boundaries gracefully, and complete clean handovers.

assessment_model.type: Document Playbook & Simulated Client Interaction Rubric Assessment
assessment_model.standards: Evaluation is based on observable communication clarity, factual accuracy, listening comprehension, structured status reports, appropriate scope-change boundaries, professional tone, and confidentiality. No scoring of real client acquisition, sales revenue, or paid software usage.

modules.title: Client Communication Foundations
modules.name: Client Communication Foundations
modules.module_purpose: Develop professional communication standards, realistic client expectations and appropriate communication boundaries.
modules.objective: Develop professional communication standards, realistic client expectations and appropriate communication boundaries.

lessons.title: Introduction to Client Communication
lessons.what_is_taught: Client-facing responsibilities across freelancing, agency environments, and service-delivery operations; distinguishing internal vs external stakeholders; communicating across the full project lifecycle.

lessons.title: Professional Tone
lessons.what_is_taught: Mastering clear language, respect, courtesy, direct communication, constructive wording, avoiding unnecessary jargon, and maintaining appropriate formality.

lessons.title: Stakeholder Awareness
lessons.what_is_taught: Identifying and communicating effectively with different project stakeholders: client sponsor, project owner, account coordinator, creative/technical team, decision-maker, approver, and external collaborator.

lessons.title: Understanding Client Expectations
lessons.what_is_taught: Aligning on project goals, scope, deliverables, timelines, quality expectations, review processes, mutual responsibilities, and ongoing communication needs.

lessons.title: Communication Channels
lessons.what_is_taught: Evaluating strengths and trade-offs of professional email, Google Meet, messaging platforms, project-management comments, shared documents, screen-recorded updates, and synchronous vs asynchronous communication.

lessons.title: Choosing the Right Channel
lessons.what_is_taught: Selecting the appropriate channel for routine status updates, clarification requests, urgent blockers, complex discussions, sensitive issues, formal approvals, and escalations.

lessons.title: Response Standards
lessons.what_is_taught: Establishing acknowledgment protocols, response expectations, business hours, urgency levels, appropriate escalation paths, realistic availability, and client-specific service agreements without universal 24h promises.

lessons.title: Professional Boundaries
lessons.what_is_taught: Setting working hours, managing availability, establishing appropriate contact channels, keeping personal vs professional accounts separate, emergency communication, and respectful refusal of unreasonable demands.

lessons.title: Cultural Awareness
lessons.what_is_taught: Navigating diverse communication styles, time zones, language preferences, direct vs indirect communication, clarity across cultures, accessible communication, and avoiding cultural stereotypes.

lessons.title: Written Communication Fundamentals
lessons.what_is_taught: Crafting action-oriented subject lines, purpose-first writing, readable paragraph structures, bulleted summaries, explicit calls to action, approved deadlines, and professional sign-offs.

lessons.title: Communication Errors
lessons.what_is_taught: Identifying and eliminating vague commitments, unclear ownership, emotional responses, overpromising, ignoring questions, excessive messaging, and premature or unnecessary escalation.

lessons.title: AI-Assisted Tone Review
lessons.what_is_taught: Using AI tools responsibly to improve message clarity, refine professional tone, enhance conciseness, detect hidden ambiguity, verify facts, and enforce human approval before sending.

modules.hands_on_lab: Rewrite five poorly communicated client messages into clear, professional responses. Create a simple communication-channel and response-expectation policy.
modules.practical_assignment: Prepare professional communication standards, preferred channels, business hours, acknowledgment rules, urgency definitions, escalation contacts/roles, and basic confidentiality guidelines.
modules.expected_deliverable: Client Communication Standards & Channel Policy (Section 1 of Client Communication Playbook)
modules.commercial_application: Freelancing, creative agencies, client services, consulting, and remote project teams.

modules.title: Onboarding & Discovery Communication
modules.name: Onboarding & Discovery Communication
modules.module_purpose: Learn to clarify client requirements, conduct productive kickoff discussions and document decisions accurately.
modules.objective: Learn to clarify client requirements, conduct productive kickoff discussions and document decisions accurately.

lessons.title: Client Onboarding Fundamentals
lessons.what_is_taught: Understanding the strategic purpose of onboarding: professional first impressions, setting expectations, explaining workflows, identifying stakeholders, and clarifying roles and responsibilities.

lessons.title: Welcome / Onboarding Messages
lessons.what_is_taught: Drafting structured welcome communications: professional greetings, project acknowledgments, immediate next steps, required assets/information, communication channels, and meeting schedules.

lessons.title: Discovery Conversations
lessons.what_is_taught: Conducting discovery conversations to uncover core client goals, business context, target audience, desired outcomes, existing assets, known constraints, and strategic priorities.

lessons.title: Requirements-Clarification Questions
lessons.what_is_taught: Formulating targeted questions: What problem should the work solve? Who is the audience? What deliverables are expected? What constraints exist? Who approves? What does success mean?
topics: What problem should this work solve?

lessons.title: Open-Ended & Closed Questions
lessons.what_is_taught: Balancing open-ended exploration with closed confirmation questions, prioritizing features, identifying unstated assumptions, avoiding leading questions, and checking comprehension.

lessons.title: Separating Facts and Assumptions
lessons.what_is_taught: Distinguishing confirmed requirements from client preferences, unanswered questions, project risks, technical dependencies, and items awaiting formal approval.

lessons.title: Defining Communication Responsibilities
lessons.what_is_taught: Designating primary contacts, client approver, internal team representative, meeting owner, decision owner, update cadence, and clarifying authorization boundaries.

lessons.title: Preparing a Kickoff Agenda
lessons.what_is_taught: Structuring an effective kickoff agenda: introductions, project objectives, scope summary, milestone schedule, team responsibilities, communication processes, dependencies, and next steps.

lessons.title: Conducting a Kickoff Call
lessons.what_is_taught: Opening meetings professionally, agenda confirmation, active listening, structured note-taking, time management, asking clarifying questions, and summarizing live decisions.

lessons.title: Google Meet Etiquette
lessons.what_is_taught: Punctuality, microphone checks, camera preferences, professional screen sharing, background noise management, access permissions, recording consent, and professional meeting closing.

lessons.title: Meeting Notes
lessons.what_is_taught: Documenting meeting purpose, date, participants, discussion summary, decisions made, open questions, action items, assigned owners, and confirmed due dates.

lessons.title: Action Items
lessons.what_is_taught: Defining specific actionable tasks, responsible assignees, confirmed deadlines, task dependencies, current status, and follow-up verification methods.

lessons.title: Post-Meeting Summary
lessons.what_is_taught: Writing concise post-meeting recaps: decisions made, action items, responsibilities, pending approvals, next meeting schedule, and explicit requests for client confirmation/correction.
topics: Action items table with owners and dates

lessons.title: Managing Unclear Requirements
lessons.what_is_taught: Spotting contradictions in client briefs, asking targeted follow-up questions, documenting unanswered issues, avoiding guesswork, and confirming details before starting work.

lessons.title: Onboarding Documentation
lessons.what_is_taught: Assembling the complete onboarding documentation kit: welcome message, discovery worksheet, kickoff agenda, meeting notes, action register, and approval checklist.

modules.hands_on_lab: Conduct a simulated client discovery and kickoff meeting using a supplied fictional brief with assigned roles: Client, Service Provider, Project Coordinator, Observer.
modules.practical_assignment: Prepare client onboarding email, discovery questions, kickoff meeting agenda, meeting summary, action-item register, and requirements clarification message.
modules.commercial_application: Freelancing projects, digital agencies, client onboarding, consulting engagements and service delivery.

modules.title: Asynchronous Updates & Coordination
modules.name: Asynchronous Updates & Coordination
modules.module_purpose: Communicate progress clearly, coordinate basic tasks and request useful feedback without unnecessary meetings.
modules.objective: Communicate progress clearly, coordinate basic tasks and request useful feedback without unnecessary meetings.

lessons.title: Synchronous vs Asynchronous Work
lessons.what_is_taught: Evaluating live meetings vs email updates, screen-recorded walkthroughs, task comments, and written documentation; identifying when each method is optimal.
topics: Written documentation as source of truth

lessons.title: Effective Project Updates
lessons.what_is_taught: Structuring high-value project updates: work completed, work currently in progress, upcoming tasks, blockers, risks, decisions required from client, and next update timing.

lessons.title: Weekly Status Report Structure
lessons.what_is_taught: Mastering the reusable industry framework: Completed → In Progress → Next → Blockers → Client Action Required with reporting period, milestones, owners, and due dates.
topics: Completed → In Progress → Next → Blockers → Client Action Required framework
Explicit next actions for client sign-off

lessons.title: Concise Professional Emails
lessons.what_is_taught: Writing concise emails: informative subject lines, short contextual framing, clear current status, explicit requests, relevant deadlines, professional tone, and crisp closings.

lessons.title: Asynchronous Screen Recording
lessons.what_is_taught: Using asynchronous video updates: purpose of the update, short overview, window selection, demonstrating progress visually, explaining specific feedback points, and stating next steps.

lessons.title: Screen Recording Best Practices
lessons.what_is_taught: Preparing speaking outlines, avoiding rambling, hiding sensitive desktop notifications, verifying display zoom and audio quality, keeping updates focused, and checking permissions.

lessons.title: Loom or Equivalent
lessons.what_is_taught: Operating screen recording tools (Loom or accessible free alternatives): recording screen with audio, reviewing outputs, sharing appropriately, managing access, and updating links.
topics: Updating or replacing links when deliverables change

lessons.title: Privacy in Recorded Updates
lessons.what_is_taught: Securing client consent where appropriate, shielding confidential files and client data, protecting internal discussions, restricting links, and revoking access when required.
topics: Protecting confidential client files and data
Shielding personal or internal team chats
Restricted link distribution vs public links

lessons.title: Basic Task Tracking
lessons.what_is_taught: Maintaining task attributes: task name, single assigned owner, target due date, current status, priority level, task dependencies, active blockers, and immediate next action.

lessons.title: Trello / Notion
lessons.what_is_taught: Building simple task boards (To Do, In Progress, Review, Completed) in Trello, Notion, or Google Sheets; assignments, task comments, and basic project status coordination.
topics: Standard workflow columns: To Do, In Progress, Review, Done
Using Google Sheets as an accessible tracker alternative

lessons.title: Slack Awareness
lessons.what_is_taught: Understanding Slack/messaging etiquette: project channels, conversation threads, respectful @mentions, status summaries, notification management, and maintaining confidentiality.
topics: Using threads to keep discussions organized

lessons.title: Feedback Requests
lessons.what_is_taught: Asking specific questions rather than vague "What do you think?", identifying exact review versions, providing context, clarifying approval needs, and requesting consolidated feedback.
topics: Identifying exact deliverable version and links

lessons.title: Documenting Feedback
lessons.what_is_taught: Logging feedback items: source stakeholder, priority level, clarification needed, assigned owner, revision status, and confirmed resolution decisions.
topics: Logging feedback items in a register

lessons.title: Avoiding Communication Overload
lessons.what_is_taught: Eliminating unnecessary meetings, reducing repeated status requests, filtering notification spam, stopping duplicated messages, consolidating fragmented feedback, and maintaining one source of truth.
topics: Proactive updates to reduce client check-ins
Maintaining a single source of truth

lessons.title: AI-Assisted Status Drafts
lessons.what_is_taught: Using AI to summarize raw task notes, format weekly reports into standard templates, improve clarity, identify missing action items, polish tone, and verify facts before sending.
topics: Summarizing raw bullet notes with AI
Formatting status reports into standard templates
Spotting missing action items or owners

modules.practical_assignment: Submit weekly progress update, professional status email, task tracking board/worksheet, structured feedback-request message, and short screen-recorded project update OR approved equivalent.

modules.title: Difficult Client Conversations
modules.name: Difficult Client Conversations
modules.module_purpose: Respond professionally to changes, delays, misunderstandings, quality concerns and difficult interactions.
modules.objective: Respond professionally to changes, delays, misunderstandings, quality concerns and difficult interactions.

lessons.title: Difficult Conversation Fundamentals
lessons.what_is_taught: Recognizing interpersonal tension, listening fully before replying, separating facts from emotions, choosing neutral language, respectful acknowledgment, and identifying core underlying problems.
topics: Recognizing early signs of client tension
Separating objective facts from emotional language
Diagnosing the root issue behind complaints

lessons.title: Professional De-Escalation
lessons.what_is_taught: Avoiding defensive responses, clarifying exact client concerns, reflecting understanding, outlining clear immediate next steps, setting healthy boundaries, and seeking workable solutions.
topics: Reflecting back understanding to build rapport

lessons.title: Scope Change vs Clarification
lessons.what_is_taught: Distinguishing agreed project scope from new feature requests, ambiguous brief clarifications, change documentation protocols, and formal change-request approval workflows.
topics: Clarifying genuine ambiguities vs scope additions

lessons.title: Communicating Scope Changes
lessons.what_is_taught: Acknowledging client requests positively, clarifying differences from original agreements, identifying impacts on schedule and budget, explaining approval requirements, and proposing options without unauthorized commitments.
topics: Clarifying the difference from the current scope
Avoiding unauthorized pricing or schedule promises

lessons.title: Revision Requests
lessons.what_is_taught: Clarifying requested changes, identifying affected deliverables, confirming deliverable versions, consolidating feedback from multiple reviewers, tracking revision progress, and confirming sign-off.
topics: Tracking revision status in the register

lessons.title: Managing Unreasonable Revision Expectations
lessons.what_is_taught: Reviewing agreed revision limits, explaining delivery constraints respectfully, offering tiered options, maintaining professionalism, documenting choices, and escalating when necessary.
topics: Escalating to project leads when appropriate

lessons.title: Missed Deadlines
lessons.what_is_taught: Informing clients promptly of potential delays, explaining verified root causes without making excuses, owning appropriate responsibility, identifying schedule impacts, proposing recovery options, and seeking revised sign-off.
topics: Early warning communication before deadlines pass

lessons.title: Communicating Quality Concerns
lessons.what_is_taught: Acknowledging client quality feedback, gathering objective evidence, documenting specific issues, evaluating severity, proposing corrective actions, and confirming resolution.
topics: Documenting specific technical or aesthetic defects
Assessing severity and impact on client goals
Proposing a concrete remediation action plan
Reviewing corrected work and confirming resolution

lessons.title: Handling Mistakes
lessons.what_is_taught: Practicing professional transparency, avoiding defensive excuses, correcting inaccurate information immediately, communicating recovery workflows, and conducting structured follow-ups.
topics: Explaining recovery workflows and preventive steps

lessons.title: Conflict Resolution
lessons.what_is_taught: Identifying competing stakeholder expectations, clarifying verified facts, active listening during heated moments, crafting professional responses, building mutual agreement, and documenting resolutions.
topics: Identifying divergent client and team expectations
Clarifying verified facts vs emotional perceptions

lessons.title: Escalation
lessons.what_is_taught: Understanding when to escalate issues, mapping decision authority, involving internal leads and senior client stakeholders, structuring objective escalation summaries with evidence and timestamps.
topics: Clear criteria for when to escalate issues
Compiling supporting evidence and communication logs

lessons.title: Professional Boundaries
lessons.what_is_taught: Respectful boundary enforcement, handling after-hours pings, managing artificial urgency, identifying harassment or abusive behavior, setting limits, and escalating unsafe interactions.

lessons.title: Cross-Cultural Sensitivity
lessons.what_is_taught: Navigating international directness, respectful phrasing across geographies, time-zone etiquette, language precision, avoiding colloquial idioms that confuse clients, and checking mutual interpretation.
topics: Adapting to direct vs indirect feedback cultures

lessons.title: Difficult Conversations by Email
lessons.what_is_taught: Drafting sensitive emails: eliminating emotional phrases, using specific subject lines, stating objective facts, writing short explanations, proposing next steps, and preserving a professional tone.

lessons.title: When to Move to a Live Conversation
lessons.lesson_title: When to Move to a Live Conversation
lessons.what_is_taught: Evaluating when to transition from email to a live call: escalating misunderstandings, complex emotional nuances, multiple unresolved items, or rapid clarification needs while respecting accessibility and preferences.
topics: Indicators that email is breaking down

lessons.title: AI-Assisted Tone Review
lessons.what_is_taught: Using AI to identify unintentional aggressive or defensive phrasing, increasing empathy and clarity, reducing ambiguity, checking factual commitments, and enforcing human review.
topics: Mandatory human review of sensitive emails

modules.hands_on_lab: Role-play three client scenarios: Scenario A (Scope Change), Scenario B (Project Delay), Scenario C (Quality Complaint).
modules.practical_assignment: Prepare written responses for: scope-change request, revision clarification, missed-deadline notice, quality complaint, conflict escalation, and professional boundary-setting.
modules.commercial_application: Agency account communication, freelancing, consulting and service-delivery coordination.

modules.title: Client Communication Capstone
modules.name: Client Communication Capstone
modules.module_purpose: Demonstrate professional communication and basic coordination across one complete simulated client project.
modules.objective: Demonstrate professional communication and basic coordination across one complete simulated client project.

lessons.title: Project Scenario Selection
lessons.what_is_taught: Selecting a realistic client simulation scenario: client business type, service category, project purpose, expected deliverables, stakeholder roster, and communication requirements.

lessons.title: Simulated Client Enquiry
lessons.what_is_taught: Executing the initial enquiry response: professional acknowledgment, information gathering requests, establishing tone, and setting up the discovery step.

lessons.title: Onboarding
lessons.what_is_taught: Delivering the formal welcome message, clarifying requirements, identifying stakeholders, and establishing the project communication protocol.

lessons.title: Kickoff
lessons.what_is_taught: Conducting the kickoff phase: agenda preparation, simulated meeting execution, meeting notes compilation, decisions record, and action items distribution.

lessons.title: Project Coordination
lessons.what_is_taught: Building and maintaining the task tracker: milestones, task owners, current status, dependencies, and project updates.
topics: Assigning task owners and due dates

lessons.title: Weekly Client Communication
lessons.what_is_taught: Producing regular weekly client updates: progress reporting, completed work review, upcoming work schedule, blockers, and required client feedback.

lessons.title: Revision Management
lessons.what_is_taught: Processing simulated client feedback: acknowledging requests, clarifying revisions, recording items in the feedback register, confirming ownership, and communicating progress.
topics: Logging changes in the feedback register

lessons.title: Difficult Conversation
lessons.what_is_taught: Handling a simulated challenge (scope change, project delay, or quality concern): professional response, impact assessment, escalation where required, and documented next steps.
topics: Managing simulated scope change or delay

lessons.title: Responsible AI Review
lessons.what_is_taught: Reviewing communication outputs with AI: draft refinement, confidentiality audit, factual accuracy check, commitment verification, cultural appropriateness, and tone.
topics: Refining drafts with AI writing tools

lessons.title: Client Handover
lessons.what_is_taught: Executing the formal handover: completion message, deliverables checklist, access/file instructions, completed actions, open items, support boundaries, and client acknowledgment request.
topics: File access and asset delivery instructions
Review of completed actions and revisions
Documenting any open or post-launch items
Defining support boundaries and warranty limits

lessons.title: Final Playbook Organization
lessons.what_is_taught: Consolidating all templates and documents into a clean, unified Client Communication Playbook: policies, onboarding, meeting notes, status reports, revision kits, escalation, and handover.

lessons.title: Final Presentation
lessons.what_is_taught: Presenting the client scenario, communication workflow, challenges encountered, decisions made, response examples, and personal reflection on lessons learned.

modules.hands_on_lab: Complete the simulated client interaction from enquiry through handover.
modules.practical_assignment: Submit one fully assembled Client Communication Playbook and one complete client interaction simulation.
modules.commercial_application: Freelance client delivery, agency coordination, consulting and project-based professional services.
